title: Levy of and Exemptions from Customs Duty
outcomes: Identify the taxable event for imports and exports.
Determine the relevant date for rate of duty.
Apply pilferage, abatement, remission and abandonment.
Apply exemption provisions and their interpretation.

meta.exam_tip: For loss questions, first fix when and how the loss occurred: pilferage, damage or total loss.

concepts.title: Customs territory and the taxable event
body: Section 12 levies customs duty on goods imported into or exported from India at rates under the Customs Tariff Act, 1975 or other law; Government goods are not exempt by default. India includes territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline, while Indian customs waters extend to the exclusive economic zone (200 nautical miles).

The charge is on the goods. For goods cleared for home consumption, import is completed when goods reach the customs barrier and a bill of entry is filed (Garden Silk Mills). For warehoused goods, import is completed on clearance from the warehouse (Apar Ltd.). Export is complete when goods cross the territorial waters.

Section 20 makes re-imported goods dutiable like fresh imports, though notifications give concessions, e.g. goods exported for repairs pay duty only on the fair cost of repairs plus freight and insurance both ways, when re-imported within the time limits.
concepts.analogy: Duty attaches to goods crossing the customs frontier.
concepts.work: Goods on a ship anchored at sea are not yet imported for duty purposes.

concepts.title: Relevant date for rate of duty
body: Section 15 fixes the date for rate of duty and tariff value. Goods for home consumption: date of presenting the bill of entry, or entry inwards of the vessel or arrival of aircraft or vehicle, whichever is later.
Goods cleared from a warehouse: date of presenting the bill of entry for home consumption for those goods. Any other goods: date of payment of duty.
A bill of entry filed before arrival is treated as presented on entry inwards. Section 15 governs only rate and tariff value; transaction value is under section 14.
concepts.analogy: Later of filing or arrival for direct clearance.
concepts.work: A rate cut after warehousing benefits goods cleared later.

concepts.title: Pilferage, abatement, remission and abandonment
body: Section 13: goods pilfered after unloading and before the clearance or warehousing order are free of duty for the importer unless restored; the custodian pays duty under section 45. It covers petty theft, not loss of whole packages.

Section 22: duty on goods damaged or deteriorated before or during unloading, or damaged by accident after unloading but before examination (or warehoused goods before clearance) without the owner's fault, is reduced in proportion of value after damage to value before. Section 23(1): duty is remitted on goods lost (other than by pilferage) or destroyed before clearance for home consumption; this covers warehoused goods too.

Section 23(2): the owner may relinquish title before the clearance or warehousing order and escape duty, unless an offence appears to have been committed. Section 24 permits denaturing or mutilation, duty then being charged as if so imported.
concepts.analogy: No duty on what is stolen, lost or abandoned in time.
concepts.work: Total loss of 500 tonnes in port custody is remission, not pilferage.

concepts.title: Exemptions from customs duty
body: Section 25(1) lets the Central Government exempt goods generally by notification, absolutely or on conditions. A conditional exemption lapses on 31 March falling immediately after two years from grant or variation, except for trade agreements, international obligations, FTP schemes, re-imports, temporary imports, gifts, baggage and similar listed cases.

Section 25(2) allows special exemptions by order in exceptional cases; section 25(6) waives duty of ₹100 or less. A notification takes effect when issued for publication in the Gazette; courts have stressed actual publication. Clarifications under section 25(2A) within one year apply retrospectively.

Sections 25A and 25B enable exemption for goods imported for processing and re-exported within one year, or exported for processing and re-imported within one year, if identifiable. The claimant proves eligibility; eligibility is read strictly, and once eligible, the benefit is read liberally (Wood Papers). The importer may choose the more beneficial notification.
concepts.analogy: Exemptions suspend collection; they do not erase the levy.
concepts.work: A conditional exemption granted in June 2025 lapses on 31 March 2028 unless extended.

illustrations.q: Kestrel Imports filed a bill of entry for home consumption on 6 July; the vessel entered inwards on 9 July. Duty was 15% until 7 July and 10% from 8 July. For a second lot warehoused on 12 July and cleared ex-warehouse on 20 November, the rate was cut to 7.5% from 1 November. State the applicable rates.

summary: Section 12 charge on goods; Government goods included.
Section 15: later of BoE or entry inwards; ex-warehouse BoE date.
Section 13 pilferage; 22 abatement; 23 remission and abandonment.
Section 25 exemptions with two-year sunset for conditional ones.
remember: Duty of ₹100 or less is not collected.

viva.q: Who pays duty on pilfered goods?
viva.model: The custodian approved under section 45 bears the duty; the importer is free unless the goods are restored.

viva.q: How does section 23 differ from section 13?
viva.model: Section 23 covers total loss or destruction, including warehoused goods, proven by the importer; section 13 covers petty theft after unloading.
Treating multi-use goods so they become unfit for some uses, after which duty applies as if imported in that form.

viva.q: Who bears the burden of proving exemption eligibility?
Are Government imports duty-free by default?
viva.model: Section 12(2) applies duty equally to Government goods; relief comes only through specific notifications.

cases.case: Of 4,000 tonnes of coal imported, 300 tonnes went missing from port custody before clearance; no sign of package tampering.

options: No, it is a large loss, not petty theft
mcqs.explain: Pilfer means petty theft. In practice: section 23.
Remission for loss. In practice: before clearance.
To the AC/DC. In practice: weighment certificate.

mcqs.q: If duty was already paid, the importer gets:
mcqs.explain: Refund follows remission. In practice: apply promptly.
